name: INT8 vocabulary scan with exact BF16 shortlist rerank
hypothesis: A lossy low-byte scan can recall a small candidate set while exact BF16 recomputation preserves the measured greedy winner at negligible cost.
expected_global_effect: Reduce batch-1 greedy TPOT while retaining bounded token identity against the exact FP8-backbone control.

preserved_dependencies: Approximate scores depend on every hidden-state element and every quantized vocabulary row.
Final shortlist scores depend on the original BF16 tied-embedding rows and the same hidden state.
changed_boundaries: Full-vocabulary BF16 evaluation is decomposed into an INT8 recall stage and a BF16 shortlist rerank stage.
The supported output boundary is greedy argmax rather than complete full-vocabulary logits.
prohibited_rewrites: Do not claim full-logit, logprob, stochastic-sampling or all-input mathematical equivalence.
Do not enable the candidate for max_num_seqs greater than one without a new service-curve qualification.
dependency_contract.numerical_ordering: Within the recalled shortlist, each token row is recomputed from original BF16 weights with FP32 reduction before greedy selection; shortlist recall remains an empirically qualified, non-certified boundary.

evidence.claim: Nsight observes both the full-vocabulary INT8 scan and exact BF16 rerank kernels once per generated step.
The frozen 512-case quality gate records 512/512 token and answer agreement.
